top.line: How agents ship native iOS apps from Linux containers, and what TestFlight and App Store review took for us.
top.para: CI on a Mac, signing once, three doors.

in-short.line: Native solved problems; CI compiles; sign once; every push to TestFlight; three doors; TestFlight is enough.

why.line: Recording, on-device models, keys and the share sheet need native; agents made native possible.
why.para: The road to phones is the hard part.

ci.line: One Mac job per push builds and tests; errors come back as text for agents; every screen is photographed.

signing.line: API key, archive unsigned, sign with entitlements, check the bundle, export and upload; CI owns build numbers.

testflight.line: Every green push uploads; a script sends builds to external testers; crash reports come back to CI.

doors.line: Internal testers about an hour; external half a day to a day; App Store still waiting after eight days.

fast.line: VoiceDebrief reached TestFlight in about an hour; a fringe guide in ten and a half hours.

prompt.line: A prompt to set the pipeline up with your own Claude.
prompt.para: Including what to do by hand.

limits.line: Timings are our experience; one App Store submission; the store step manual; device tests need a person.

sources.line: The VoiceDebrief and PrompTugal iOS repositories, my own experience, earlier articles.
